problem_type: Stale public community destination after GitHub repository setting changed
symptom: The SEO contract test fails because it still asserts that an active repository Discussions URL must be absent, while the current GitHub repository exposes a working Discussions page and the marketing website still labels Issues as the community destination.
direct_cause: The former repository setting was encoded as a negative assertion, and the marketing source retained an Issues destination after Discussions was enabled externally.
class_root: There is no enforced invariant that all active public community surfaces use one verified, current GitHub destination while keeping issue reporting as a separate surface.
affected_population: Users arriving through the English or Chinese README
Users choosing the repository contact link before opening an issue
Users following the English model-connection tutorial
Search crawlers and link-preview consumers reading public repository and marketing content
entry_points: Marketing content source and generated bilingual pages
SEO and marketing static contract tests

external_sources.purpose: Verify that the canonical Discussions destination is currently enabled, reachable, and populated.

invariants: Bug reports and feature requests continue to use the Issues surface.
Generated marketing pages and their content source remain in sync.
generality_proof: Repository-wide search found the active README, issue-template, guide, marketing source, generated pages, and tests as the independent surfaces that expose the community destination. The updated static gate checks the active user-facing documents together, so a future repository-setting or copy change cannot silently leave the marketing pages on a contradictory URL. Historical plans, specs, and mockups are excluded because they document prior decisions rather than active entry points.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the canonical marketing community destination used to generate both localized public pages.

shared_boundaries.symbol: public community links resolve to a real GitHub surface
shared_boundaries.responsibility: Enforce the current active-surface destination contract across source documents and prevent stale-link drift.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: English repository community and contribution links
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Repository-wide search found three active community/contribution references; the test checks that the README retains the canonical Discussions destination.
The Chinese README is an indexed repository entry point and already had the verified Discussions URL; it is now included in the active-surface assertion.
GitHub renders this configuration before issue creation, so it is an active user-facing community entry point and already targets the verified Discussions surface.
The guide is linked from the public README and already contains the verified Discussions destination for setup questions and follow-up.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: Desktop bug and feature issue submission
same_class_entry_points.evidence: This path intentionally reports reproducible bugs and feature requests to Issues; it is not a general community discussion destination.

recurrence.reason: GitHub repository settings can change independently of commits, and the community destination is duplicated across generated source, READMEs, configuration, guides, and tests. Without a positive active-surface invariant, the same drift can recur after a future setting or copy change.
same_class_scan: rg -n -i 'github\.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/(discussions|issues)|GitHub Discussions|/discussions' across active repository, marketing, guide, and test paths.
Checked scripts/marketing/content.mjs and generated marketing/index.html plus marketing/en/index.html.
Checked README.md, README.zh-CN.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml, and docs/guide/model-connection-en.md; these already use Discussions.
Checked src/ui/community/communityLinks.ts and retained its Issues-only reporting role as not affected.

prevention.invariant: Every active public/community surface must contain the verified canonical Discussions URL, and active generated marketing content must not silently diverge from it.
prevention.failure_mode: The SEO contract test fails before delivery when an active surface omits the canonical destination or reintroduces a contradictory stale destination.
prevention.strategy: Keep the canonical destination in the marketing content source and assert the full active-surface set in one static test; keep issue-reporting code outside that set with an explicit not-affected disposition.

legacy_paths.rationale: The obsolete Issues-only community copy is removed from active marketing source and generated pages where Discussions is the verified current destination. Historical plans, specs, mockups, and issue-reporting code are intentionally retained because they describe prior decisions or a different user intent.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime controls this invariant; the failure is caused by repository-state drift and duplicated public copy.

migration: No persisted data or runtime state is involved. Regenerate the marketing HTML from scripts/marketing/content.mjs and update active Markdown/YAML links in the same change.
residual_risks: GitHub can disable Discussions again without a repository commit; the static gate cannot prove external settings at every future run, so the verified external source and periodic SEO observatory remain necessary.
Keyword demand, ranking, backlink, and AI-visibility opportunities remain unmeasured until an authorized OpenSEO/DataForSEO connection is provided.
